title: Pipe or editor?
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Should a platform pass on every word, or choose which words travel?

Jose said that one of the people who built the payments company with the person in the book put a question to him about the social network he was buying: should it be like a telephone system, where the words that go in one end come out exactly the same on the other? Or a system that governs the discourse of the world, with some intelligence in the algorithm that prioritizes or deprioritizes things?
Jose asked each student where they would be. A student said: I would probably be at option one, the telephone, but I see how businesses might want the other. Another said: I lean to option one.

Jose said he would play devil's advocate, just for fun: someone might say people need to be guided because a society can be too irresponsible if you let people roam free. He gave an analogy with a child who says whatever he wants, and swears. As a responsible adult, he said, do you have a responsibility to say: that is irresponsible?
A student said: a parent governing a child and a government censoring adults are apples and oranges. Another said: who becomes the measurer of responsible speech? That is a pretty ugly rabbit hole.
Jose said: that is why I want to go down it. We have to think about it. Where is the line?

A student said: when a government has the power of filtering what should be allowed, we are not looking at the audience. A child's programmes are for an older audience. But a government shutting down things that could be of value to the masses is another matter.

Jose asked: what about classified military information? Shouldn't that be free? A student said: withholding information is not the same as censoring what someone says. Jose said: there is a very thin line between the two.

A student gave a business example: you plan to acquire or sell a company, so you discuss it with a few key people. You keep it confidential until you are comfortable disclosing your intentions. There is always a point in time when you keep it to a tight circle.
Jose said: intention is a big part of it. A student said: but who becomes the measurer of intention? Jose said: and who is right, whose value system?
What would you want a platform to do with your own words?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write whether you want a platform to pass on everything or choose.
Write who should decide what is responsible speech.
Write the difference between confidential and censored in your work.
Write what you keep confidential and until when.
Write how you would decide on a case where you aren't sure.

check.q: What was the question about the social network?
choices: A telephone system, or a system that governs the discourse of the world

check.q: What did a student ask about responsible speech?
What did a student say a business keeps confidential?
choices: A planned acquisition, until the right moment

recap: Think about pipe or editor. Tell confidential from censored. Ask who measures.
